answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit that only unlocks after sustained honest work, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. Reputation should echo across trades: a whisper of distrust from verified counterparties travels faster than praise, and bad actors fall into a trust canyon that takes real work to climb out of. Stake plus peer attestation plus slow reputation recovery makes fakes cost more than they earn.
